question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The postman said, "I deliver parcels to this colony every Tuesday and Friday."
option_1: The postman said that he delivers parcels to that colony every Tuesday and Friday.
option_2: The postman said that he is delivering parcels to that colony every Tuesday and Friday.
option_3: The postman said that he delivered parcels to that colony every Tuesday and Friday.
option_4: The postman said that he has delivered parcels to that colony every Tuesday and Friday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The postman said that he delivered parcels to that colony every Tuesday and Friday.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A habitual personal routine expressed in the simple present ("deliver") backshifts to the simple past ("delivered") when reported with a past-tense reporting verb, and the demonstrative "this" shifts to "that".

◦ Complete sentence: The postman said that he delivered parcels to that colony every Tuesday and Friday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...he delivers parcels..." — the simple present is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to the simple past.

 

• Option 2: "...he is delivering parcels..." — the continuous aspect is wrongly introduced, changing the sense of the original statement.

 

• Option 4: "...he has delivered parcels..." — the present perfect is wrongly used instead of the simple past "delivered".

 

NOTE

 

• She said, "I water these plants every morning." → she said that she watered those plants every morning (habitual simple present → simple past, in backshifting).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

 

The supervisor ordered the workers to switch off all machines before leaving.
option_1: The supervisor said to the workers, "Switching off all machines before leaving."
option_2: The supervisor said the workers, "Switch off all machines before leaving."
option_3: The supervisor said to the workers, "You must switch off all machines before leaving."
option_4: The supervisor said to the workers, "Switch off all machines before leaving."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The supervisor said to the workers, "Switch off all machines before leaving.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An order reported with "ordered...to" un-backshifts to the plain imperative form in direct speech: "Switch off all machines before leaving."

◦ Complete sentence: The supervisor said to the workers, "Switch off all machines before leaving."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Switching off all machines..." — the gerund fragment is not a valid imperative; the direct command must be "Switch off all machines".

 

• Option 2: "The supervisor said the workers..." — the preposition "to" is missing; it should be "said to the workers".

 

• Option 3: "...You must switch off..." — the modal "must" is an unwarranted addition; the original order un-backshifts to a plain imperative, not a modal statement.

 

NOTE

 

• The captain ordered the sailors to lower the sails immediately. → the captain said to the sailors, "Lower the sails immediately." (ordered...to → plain imperative, in un-backshifting).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The judge asked the witness, "Where were you standing when the incident occurred?"
option_1: The judge asked the witness where was he standing when the incident occurred.
option_2: The judge asked the witness where he had been standing when the incident occurred.
option_3: The judge asked the witness where he was standing when the incident had occurred.
option_4: The judge asked the witness that where he had been standing when the incident occurred.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The judge asked the witness where he had been standing when the incident occurred.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a wh-question, statement word order replaces the interrogative order, and of the two past actions, the earlier one ("were standing") takes the past perfect ("had been standing") while the later one ("occurred") remains in the simple past.

◦ Complete sentence: The judge asked the witness where he had been standing when the incident occurred.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...where was he standing..." — the interrogative word order is wrongly retained instead of the statement order "where he had been standing".

 

• Option 3: "...he was standing when the incident had occurred." — the tenses are wrongly swapped; the earlier action ("standing") should take the past perfect, not the later action ("occurred").

 

• Option 4: "...that where he had been standing..." — the superfluous connector "that" is wrongly added before the wh-word.

 

NOTE

 

• He asked, "What were you doing when the alarm rang?" → he asked what I had been doing when the alarm rang (earlier ongoing action → past perfect continuous; later action stays simple past).
